title: MedNeXt localizes mandibular cancer invasion in a small retrospective CT cohort
summary: A single-center study trained a 3D MedNeXt model within nnU-Net on 30 CT examinations and evaluated it on 20 held-out patients with histopathologically confirmed mandibular invasion by oral squamous cell carcinoma. Predicted invasion overlapped expert-reviewed CT references in 18 of 20 examinations; mean invasion Dice was 0.553 and recall 0.483, with two cases missed. Among 18 evaluable cases, median absolute longitudinal invasion-span difference was 7.01 mm. This is a retrospective localization/segmentation study among invasion-positive patients, not an assessment of specificity, surgical outcomes or clinical benefit. Larger multicenter and prospective planning studies remain necessary.
ai_technology: 3D MedNeXt convolutional network in nnU-Net v2; TotalSegmentator preprocessing
organization: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich; University of Freiburg

evidence.tested: 50 positive-patient CT examinations, 30 development and 20 single-center held-out tests; expert-reviewed radiological references. Invasion overlapped 18/20, mean Dice 0.553, precision 0.742 and recall 0.483.
evidence.unknown: No invasion-negative controls, histological voxel-level boundary reference, external-center or prospective surgical/planning outcome validation. All test patients had confirmed invasion; localization overlap does not establish diagnostic specificity or resection safety.
evidence.ai_role: MedNeXt learned image-to-mask segmentation from expert-reviewed CTimages and estimated invasion location/extent; TotalSegmentator supplied initial mandibular cropping.

source_review.scope: Primary full publisher Methods/data partitioning/model training, Results, Discussion/limitations and publication metadata; abstract. No supplement review or independent image adjudication.
